title: Sequential composition across a state seam
statement: Let $\Gamma,S_1,S_2$ be types, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $x$ be an input word over $\Gamma$. Let $M_1,M_2$ be machines with $k$ work tapes and state sets $S_1,S_2$, respectively, with decidable equality on $S_1$. Suppose $M_1$ runs from configuration $a$ to configuration $b$ in $t_1$ steps, with state $q_1$ at $b$ and no earlier occurrence of that state; suppose every work-tape head during this run stays within distance $B$ of a specified origin. Suppose also that $M_2$, started from $b$ with its state renamed to the entry state, reaches configuration $c$ in $t_2$ steps, with state $q_2$ at $c$ and no earlier occurrence of that state, and that its work-tape heads stay within distance $B$ of the same origin. Then the machine that switches from $M_1$ to $M_2$ at state $q_1$ reaches the state-renamed configuration $c$ after $t_1+1+t_2$ steps, does not reach state $q_2$ in the second component earlier, and keeps every work-tape head within distance $B$ of the origin through that time.
hypotheses_covered: $M_1$ does not have state $q_1$ at any earlier time
$M_2$ reaches $c$ from the entry-renamed $b$ after $t_2$ steps
$M_2$ does not have state $q_2$ at any earlier time
$M_2$ head-displacement bound $B$ from the same origin
